editor_note: Entry 10 is faithful. It keeps the little-endian default against BitArray's `big` default, keeps the condition "selon que la primitive modifie ou non ce paramètre", and keeps the contrast between Sampler/Estimator returning big-endian and Executor returning little-endian ("alors que Executor renvoie des résultats little-endian").

The 7 rewritten headings are faithful, natural infinitive headings: "Surveiller les paramètres", "Surveiller de manière globale", "Calibrer", and benchmark rendered as "Évaluer les performances" (a defensible heading form next to the body's "benchmarking").

The meaning holds across all 7 rewritten entries (5–11), and nothing in them would mislead a learner. The method list (PEC, PEA, TREX, ZNE par repliement de portes), the post-selection caveat, the noise-learning workflow and the tutu register are all faithful. Three phrasings are calqued from English. Entry 6 has "construits au-dessus du cadre", a literal copy of "built on top of". Entry 10 has "a eu sa première version", a stiff copy of "had its first release", and "encodages fermion-vers-qubit", which mirrors the English hyphenation. A French technical writer would rephrase all three.

editor_note: Entries 5-10 are faithful and read naturally. Each technical term is correct ("atténuation des erreurs de mesure", "mesures en milieu de circuit", "méthodes de transpilation standard, riches en SWAP"), the house-style names stay in English ("Circuit function", "Application function", "Qiskit Functions"), and the "tu" register holds ("Consulte").

Entry 5 is faithful and natural: it keeps the "tu" register ("Que tu migres vers les nouveaux Sampler et Estimator côté client"), renders skills as "compétences" to match the rest of the page, and keeps the "officielles, vérifiées par IBM" qualifier and the "dans un avenir proche" promise.

Entry 129 matches the English: "atténuation d'erreurs", "variantes de circuit randomisées", "primitive Executor" and "Qiskit Runtime" are all correct, the client-side/server-side split is kept, and it stays in "tu".

The 10 rewritten entries are faithful and nothing in them would mislead a learner. The method lists (PEC, PEA, TREX, ZNE par repliement de portes), the "in most cases, only change your imports" caveat and the informal "tu" register all carry over correctly. Two small slips remain. "built on top of" is calqued as "construites au-dessus de/du cadre" in entries 5 and 8, where a French writer would say "reposant sur" or "construits sur". Entry 12 also misses the elision before a vowel ("de Executor" should be "d'Executor").

editor_note: The French is faithful and reads naturally, and the tu register holds throughout. Key meanings survive intact: the Heron/Nighthawk conditional versus unconditional reset footnote ("la réinitialisation dépend du résultat de la mesure" / "inconditionnelle"), the DC/AC TLS bias trade-off, and the decoherence caveat on slow cz gates ("ce qui provoque un peu de décohérence supplémentaire"). Terms are used consistently: calibration alternative, atténuation des erreurs, cible (target), transpileur.

Entry 24 is faithful and reads naturally. It keeps the "tu" register ("consulte", "N'hésite pas"), uses "référence API" consistently with entry 31, and "dépôt GitHub" correctly renders "GitHub repository".

All 10 rewritten entries say what the English says. The beta admonition, the "high-level explanations" intro and every "Tu peux activer … de plusieurs manières" list keep their conditions ("si tu utilises IBM Quantum Estimator"), and entry 42 keeps the point that PEA needs ZNE enabled. The one slip is the article on the acronyms. The rest of the page writes "la ZNE" / "la PEA" / "la PEC", but the rewritten entries 35, 42 and 52 drop it ("activer ZNE", "Comme PEA est", "activer PEC"). Entry 42 also has the slightly clumsy "technique d'amplification du bruit de ZNE". Nothing here would mislead a learner.

editor_note: The 22 rewritten entries say the same as the English: "Twirling de Pauli" matches the "twirling de portes" used elsewhere, "(il faut aussi activer ZNE)" keeps the PEA prerequisite, the v0.50.0 note keeps "un job d'apprentissage du bruit distinct est nécessaire pour utiliser PEA et PEC", and the link text "Paramètres de gestion du bruit personnalisés" matches the heading in [47].

Rewritten entry 43 is faithful and keeps the informal register ("consulte la [référence API `qiskit-ibm-runtime`] et sélectionne une version précédente"), with the "dernière version" / "versions d'options antérieures" contrast preserved.

Entry 54 is a faithful translation in the "tu" register: all five bullets are kept, "directed execution model" becomes "modèle d'exécution dirigée" as in entry 7's link context, and "techniques de mitigation d'erreurs" matches the "mitigation PEC" wording in entry 29.

The four rewritten entries (32, 34–36) match the English. "least-significant bit" is rendered correctly as "le bit de poids faible", the shapes (28, 10, 1024, 3) and (28, 10, 1, 3) are kept exactly, and the tu register holds ("Note que…").

Entry 11 is faithful and natural: "ne peut traiter que les informations encodées dans des samplexes" keeps the English restriction, and "Consulte les guides Samplomatic" uses the informal tu register correctly.

Both rewritten tables are faithful overall. Every quantity, comparison and caveat survives, including the HI-VQE "respectively, by orders of magnitude" clause and the 40–60 qubit range. In entry 15, the Optimization Solver's "Noise-aware" became "sensible au bruit", which a French reader takes as "vulnerable to noise", and the Portfolio Optimizer row silently drops "noise-aware" from its error mitigation techniques. Entry 12 mixes "mitigation d'erreurs" (TEM, QESEM) with "atténuation des erreurs de mesure" (Orbit) in the same table. In HI-VQE, "avec une précision chimique" is a loose rendering of "achieving chemical accuracy".

editor_note: Entry 42 is faithful and reads naturally. The fermionic-to-bosonic logic is intact: "soumis à l'antisymétrie par échange", "système discernable ou bosonique" and "à la fois hermitiens et unitaires" all match the English, and "mapping" and "transformation de Jordan-Wigner" are used the same way as in the rest of the file.

I compared every entry and found no semantic drift. Negations, quantities and caveats are kept, including the CPC detection rule, the gamma caveats, the "B0 raw vs post" reading and the no-unbiasedness caveat. Terminology is not consistent within the file. "Check" starts as "vérification" in [0]–[26] and becomes "contrôle" from [33] on, and the references in [308] go back to "Vérifications de Pauli cohérentes". The register also slips from "tu" to "vous" in Part 1: "Exécutez" [51], "Appliquez" [52], "Utilisez" [54], "Analysez" [114], "pensez" [154] and the "Vérifiez votre compréhension" headings, while later headings use "Vérifie ta compréhension". editor_note: Entry [253] makes a stronger claim than the English. "Because PEC might only be used on a subcircuit" becomes "Comme PEC ne peut être utilisée que sur un sous-circuit", which says PEC can be used only on subcircuits. That contradicts [240] ("often applied to") and the later sections that run built-in PEC on whole 6- and 30-qubit circuits. There are also several minor problems. "Mitigation" is rendered "mitigation" up to about [405] and "atténuation" from [405] to the end ([419], [420], [424], [429], [442], [444]). The register mixes vous and tu: "Notez" in [17], [21], [32], [33], [52] and [107], "Considérez" in [42] and "vous savez" in [61] sit alongside tu elsewhere. The decimal separator also switches from French commas ("54,5 %" in [97]) to points ("86.4 %" in [372] and [387], "2.9 %" in [141]). Smaller points are the calque "carte de bruit inverse" in [415], where the file elsewhere uses "application", and "plutôt que" in [260], which turns a contrast into a preference.

editor_note: Entry 18 keeps the English meaning, including the safety caveat ("Tant que tu ne l'as pas fait, la cellule n'enregistre rien, donc exécuter toutes les cellules ne peut jamais écraser un compte que tu as enregistré auparavant"), with correct step numbers 4 and 5 and the informal "tu" throughout.

The three rewritten titles are faithful and idiomatic: [23] "Optimisation multi-objectif approchée quantique" matches the file's own QAOA title in [20], [37] "Tomographie par ombres de l'état de Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger" uses an accepted rendering of shadow tomography, and [38] "modèle d'Ising à champ transverse" matches [59].

I found no meaning errors in the 60 rewritten entries. The Fortran section is faithful: the variational bound in 204, the per-step versus pooled restriction in 209, and the discard-versus-repair contrast in 220 and 221 all match the English. The problems are consistency and register. Entry 168 uses formal "Votre", while 10 and the rest of the Fortran section use "tu". The same terms are rendered several ways: "workflow" versus "flux de travail" (the 186 link reads "Vérifier le flux de travail localement" but its target heading 202 reads "Vérifier le workflow en local"), "bindings" (198, 199) versus "liaisons" (170), "bitstrings" (173, 200, 208) versus "chaîne de bits" (181), and "pool" in the Fortran part versus "réservoir" in the Python part. Entry 206 also restructures "the reference determinant's diagonal matrix element" awkwardly.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries (18, 65, 71) keep the English meaning, with no drift or added claims, and the "tu" register holds. Two small fluency problems remain. In entry 71, "lors de sa fourniture à Executor" is a stiff nominal calque of "when providing it to Executor". In entry 65, "dans le cas de PEC" drops the article that the rest of the page uses ("la PEC"), which reads as unidiomatic and inconsistent.

The meaning holds throughout. The caveats that the tutorial does not show quantum advantage ([21], [43], [55]) and that the 40-asset run changes nothing else in the method ([46]) are all carried over faithfully. Three small slips remain. In [36] the qubit being "on" is rendered as « actif », the same word the page uses for "asset" everywhere else, so the sentence can read ambiguously. In [34], "de exactement" is missing the required elision "d'exactement". MPS is rendered as "simulateur d'états de produit matriciel" ([11], [47], [53]), which is understandable but less idiomatic than the usual "états produits matriciels".

examples.why: « actif » is the page's word for "asset", so using it for the qubit's on-state can be read as "asset" here.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The problem is terminology: from entry [67] on, the page switches to a different set of terms from the first half. "Tomographie par ombres", "ombre" and "instantanés" ([0]–[63]) become "tomographie de shadow", "shadow" and "snapshots" ([67]–[87]). Likewise "aimantation" becomes "magnétisation" ([67], [69]), "codes espace-temps" ([8], [12]) becomes "codes spacetime" ([76], [90]), and "vecteur d'état" becomes "statevector" ([75]). "Le scaling du nombre de shots" ([71], [72]) is also an anglicism that a native editor would rephrase.

examples.translation: Définis l'estimateur de shadow ... afin de collecter les snapshots de shadow ... la magnétisation à un seul Qubit
examples.suggested: Définis l'estimateur d'ombre ... afin de collecter les instantanés d'ombre ... l'aimantation à un qubit
examples.why: Earlier entries ([6], [17], [42], [63]) use 'ombre', 'instantanés' and 'aimantation', so these concepts get two names on the same page.

examples.why: 'Tomographie de shadow' conflicts with the title's 'tomographie par ombres', and 'scaling' is an untranslated anglicism.

editor_note: The 86 rewritten entries keep the meaning of the English. Numbers, conditions and caveats are intact, including 1137 of 10000 shots (about 11%), 49 of 120 α-déterminants, 0.1373 Ha above exact FCI, "Cela n'a **pas** été vérifié sur Linux" and the order-of-normalization warning. Three small things remain. The step headings are capitalized inconsistently: "Étape 1 : associer…" and "Étape 2 : construire…" are lowercase after the colon, while "Étape 3 : Exécuter…" and "Étape 4 : Post-traiter…" are capitalized. "chaque terme du groupe est évolué" is a calque of the English passive. Entry 132's "transforme ces ensembles en l'ensemble de circuits" uses "ensemble" twice in two different senses, which reads awkwardly.

examples.translation: Étape 3 : Exécuter à l'aide des primitives Qiskit (C++)
examples.suggested: Étape 3 : exécuter à l'aide des primitives Qiskit (C++)
examples.why: Entries 119 and 133 use lowercase after the colon, but 137 and 141 are capitalized. The step headings should all follow one convention.

examples.why: 'Ensemble' appears twice in two different senses (set vs. ensemble), and 'en l'ensemble' is clumsy.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the closing trade-off paragraph [67]: δt = 0.125 has the smallest Trotter error but agrees worse than 0.25. Terminology is correct and consistent (valeurs moyennes, aimantation alternée, réseau de tenseurs, trotterisé, dimension de liaison). The register slips into the formal "Notez que" three times ([36], [51], [54]), while [20] correctly uses "Note que". Two small fluency slips: "sur toutes les shots" in [56] gives the anglicism "shots" the feminine (the usual French is "tous les shots"), and "un pas moitié moindre" in [67] is stiff.
